title: Manohar Paluri Leaves Meta After 14 Years to Co-Found Warp Sciences
excerpt: The IIIT Hyderabad graduate and former Meta AI vice president is now CTO of Warp Sciences, which raised $215 million to build AI-and-robotics chemistry labs for drug discovery in the US.
body:
• Manohar "Mano" Paluri, a vice president at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a founding member of Meta's FAIR research organisation, has left after about 14 years to co-found Warp Sciences as chief technology officer.
  • Warp Sciences emerged from stealth on October 22 with $215 million in funding led by Lightspeed, at a reported $865 million post-money valuation, to build a US-based chemistry contract research organisation using AI and robotics.
  • Paluri co-founded the San Francisco startup with former OpenAI product chief Kevin Weil, former US chief data scientist DJ Patil and medicinal chemist Solomon Reisberg; Premji Invest is among the backers.
  • Warp is not developing its own drugs: biotech and pharma customers keep control of their programmes while Warp makes and tests the molecules they need.

Manohar Paluri has left Meta after about 14 years to co-found Warp Sciences, a San Francisco startup that wants to speed up drug discovery by combining expert chemists with artificial intelligence and robotics. Paluri, known as Mano Paluri at the new company, serves as chief technology officer. He was a vice president at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a founding member of FAIR, Meta's Fundamental AI Research organisation, according to the company's launch announcement.

Warp emerged from stealth on October 22 with $215 million in funding to build a US-based chemistry contract research organisation, or CRO. Lightspeed led the round, with participation from Premji Invest, Mayfield, IVP, Lux, Conviction and Menlo Ventures, among others. Bloomberg reporting put the post-money valuation at $865 million, according to Drug Development and Delivery's summary.

From IIIT Hyderabad to Meta's AI leadership

Paluri graduated from the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, with a BTech in computer science in 2006, according to a Times of India profile. He worked on computer vision at Sarnoff, pursued postgraduate work at Georgia Tech, and had research experience at IBM Watson Labs and Google before joining Facebook in 2012 as a computer vision researcher. He rose to director of AI in 2015, senior director in 2021 and vice president of AI in 2024.

https://x.com/PlusPointIndia/status/2115677508985405637

His co-founders cover the other disciplines Warp needs. Kevin Weil, the chief executive, was OpenAI's chief product officer and vice president of science. Solomon "Sol" Reisberg, the chief scientific officer, held medicinal chemistry leadership roles at Terremoto Biosciences. DJ Patil, the chief operating officer, was a founding executive at Devoted Health and the first US chief data scientist in the White House.

What Warp will actually do

Warp's first service is lead optimisation analog synthesis: making variations of a promising molecule so scientists can compare them and refine a drug candidate. The company's model is a closed loop in which experimental data trains better AI, better AI powers more capable labs, and scientists can test more ideas. The startup starts with about 20 employees and has bought robotic arms and AI chips; reporting on the launch said chemists' work may be captured with wearable cameras and sensor gloves to create training data.

"Our goal is simple: every experiment should make the next one smarter. AI needs a closer connection to the physical work of chemistry."

— Mano Paluri, Co-founder and CTO, Warp Sciences

Paluri said Warp is building the software, AI and robotics alongside the laboratory so each part is shaped by what chemists actually need. Weil made the broader case in the launch announcement: AI has accelerated software and mathematics, but chemistry and biology advance only when something is made, tested and learned from.

Why the location matters

Warp is also selling geography and intellectual-property protection. A 2024 Biotechnology Innovation Organization survey cited by the company found 74% of respondents had contracts with Chinese companies for preclinical or clinical services. The BIOSECURE Act, signed in December 2025, created a framework for restrictions on federal procurement and funding involving designated biotechnology companies of concern. Reisberg said he had worried about protecting IP with overseas partners and that Warp aims to offer US chemistry services without the price premium of US boutique CROs.

Patil stressed the boundary of the business: customers decide which molecules to pursue and retain control of their drug programmes. Warp has no proprietary drug pipeline.

What to watch next

The test for Paluri's move is execution, not funding. Warp must show that automated labs can match established CROs on speed, cost and reliability while generating data that genuinely improves its models. If it does, the career path it represents — from social-media AI research to physical-science infrastructure — will become a template for senior Indian American technologists leaving large platforms to build AI companies in regulated, real-world industries. Readers can follow the company's hiring and services at Warp's careers page, a link carried in its launch announcement.
